doc.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021

title: Gear: Jody Jazz DB Beatbox mouthpiece and slap-tongue mechanics
summary: How slap tongue affects mouthpiece choice and the custom mouthpiece made for him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well I see a tenor behind you.
There it is. It’s always behind me everywhere I go.
Did you have to fuss with your gear so that your gear helped you get where you wanted to go with the way you play?

Yeah a little bit. I mean I love saying that like man, it’s the player that makes the music, it’s not getting the right gear that’s going to make you sound better. That is so, so true. And I could do this BeatBox stuff on any horn. But there are certain things that maybe this Jody Jazz mouthpiece is a little easier, or I like the feeling of the New Mechanics. There are some small things like the fact that, this would get really technical, I won’t go all the way there, but when you slap tongue on the sax, my tongue is making a suction on the reed and it’s pulling down the reed and releasing, and you’re hearing the sound of the reed slap against the tip of the mouth piece. You can also go [tongue slaps sax] and get that kind of snare sound, but that’s the sound of the reed slapping against the mouthpiece. And most typical jazz mouthpieces are really, they have a big tip opening. And so when you do that it’s just much more tiring to do that, plus to get that sound you have to bite down on the reed. It’s kind of like a slingshot. You have to put pressure against it and so when you release it it slaps. If you do that with a really open mouthpiece the pitch is going to go way up, and so a lot of my earlier career I was fighting with out-of-tuneness where my slap tongue notes were really sharp and tiring. And so over the years I’ve been trying to find kind of the perfect mouthpiece where it’s a smaller tip opening but still gives me that power I need. Actually Jody Espina of Jody Jazz made me a specific mouthpiece, they call it the DB Beatbox, even though it makes it sound like, “Ooh if I get this I’ll be able to Beatbox on the saxophone like Derek.” It’s just a normal mouthpiece, it has a smaller tip opening but it works, it’s just good for me.
